title: Login sessions: one box renamed three times, arrow labels and a note rewritten
persona: A full-stack developer, before asking the agent why users get logged out after every deploy, sketching where they think a login session lives.
topic: where a logged-in session actually lives
realism: Finding the right word is how people find the right model: calling it 'Cache' implies a fallback on miss, and noticing that is wrong ('if it's gone you're logged out') changes another arrow too. The renames carry the reasoning; the final names alone look like they were always known.

steps.say: This is about where a logged-in session actually lives.
The browser sends the cookie with every request to the API.
The API looks the session up in the cache.
And if it's not in the cache it falls back to Postgres.
Hmm, no, that's not right, it's not really a cache, if it's gone you're logged out.
So it's the session store, and Postgres is only for loading the user row.
Sessions expire after thirty minutes, I think.
The lookup is literally a GET on sess colon the session id.
Actually I think the TTL slides, it gets reset when you make a request.
And to be concrete, the session store is Redis, its own instance, not the shared one.
I'm confident about that part, so it gets a solid line.
What I don't get is why a deploy logs everyone out, maybe something flushes Redis.
Let me move this note down so it's not in the way.

relabel.label: TTL 30 min sliding, reset on each request

steps.note: users get logged out after every deploy - is it the flush or the cookie signing key?

steps.say: Or maybe it's the migration step that flushes it, I'm really not sure which.

final_labels: TTL 30 min sliding, reset on each request
story: The box now called 'Redis (sessions)' is one element renamed twice: 'Cache' (drawn ~0:12) -> 'Session store' (~0:29) -> 'Redis (sessions)' (~1:02).

The first rename was a change of model, not of wording: it is not a cache because losing it logs you out, so the API -> Postgres arrow changed from 'on miss' to 'load user' at the same time; Postgres holds users, not a session fallback.
The second rename made it concrete (its own Redis instance, not the shared one), and the box went from dashed to solid blue because they became confident.
The API -> session store arrow was relabelled from 'lookup' to 'GET sess:<id>', and Browser -> API from 'cookie' to 'session id cookie' (that one silently).
The TTL text was edited twice: 'TTL 30 min?' -> 'TTL 30 min, sliding?' -> 'TTL 30 min sliding, reset on each request', and was moved below Postgres.
The open question is why deploys log everyone out: the dashed red Deploy -> Redis arrow went from 'flush?' to 'FLUSHDB on migrate?', and the typed note also suspects the cookie signing key.
partner_should_ask_about: whether a deploy flushes Redis or rotates the cookie signing key
whether the TTL really slides on each request
